name: render: a group's own colHeaders are ignored
why: Without the generalised branch every group clones the first group's header row (Artists'), misaligning Places, Recordings, URLs, … — the default for multi-table pages.
grep: each with its own aligned columns

name: fetch loop: colHeaders only copied for user-ratings
why: The table's data-mb-col-headers never reaches group.colHeaders, so the render falls back to the shared header.
grep: each with its own aligned columns

name: disk: colHeaders not saved
why: A Load from Disk would rebuild every group's header from the first group's.

name: disk: colHeaders not restored
why: Same, on the load side.

name: disk: the converter does not run before hydration
why: The reloaded page holds the native relationship lists again; they would stay beside the restored tables.

name: parser: the disambiguation joins the credits
why: span.comment must land in Disambiguation, not in Credits/Details.
grep: each part of a target line lands in its own column

name: parser: no artist credit
why: " by <bdi>…</bdi>" after a recording must become the Artist column.
grep: each part of a target line lands in its own column

name: parser: no area for a place
why: " in <area chain>" after a place must become the Area column.
grep: each part of a target line lands in its own column

name: parser: credits keep their parentheses
why: "(time: …, lead vocals)" is shown as the Credits value, without the wrapping pair.
grep: each part of a target line lands in its own column

name: parser: a URL loses its [info] link
why: The /url/<id> page link belongs with the URL it describes.
grep: each part of a target line lands in its own column

name: setting ignored: one table
why: "One table for all relationships" must give a single table with Type and From.

name: setting ignored: related series
why: With the setting off, the series' own relationships stay native.

name: native series section: its h3 stays an h3
why: renderGroupedTable()'s initial cleanup removes every h3 in #content, so the series name would vanish from the section left native.

name: '#' is not an integer column
why: The declaration gives '#' its right-aligned, tabular-figure cells. Numeric SORTING does not depend on it: _sortColumnKind()'s name heuristic already treats any header containing '#' as numeric.

name: button shown with every table part off
why: It would render nothing.

name: WIP.2 button: the setlist alone does not count
why: With relationships off and the setlist on, the button still has a use.

name: WIP.2 billing: '&' starts a new group too
why: "Bruce Springsteen & The E Street Band" is one billing.

name: WIP.2 'Billing' is not an integer column
why: The declaration gives Billing its right-aligned, tabular cells.

name: WIP.2 no part headers
why: A comment after a blank line names the next part; without that every song lands in one part.

name: WIP.2 a note becomes a song row
why: "Scheduled: …" describes the part; it must not be counted as a song.

name: WIP.2 a medley keeps only its first work
why: A medley line is one row listing every work it names.

name: WIP.2 'Also in' names the row's own part
why: Only the OTHER parts that play a work of the line belong there.

name: WIP.2 no recording cross-reference
why: A song with a recording made at this event links it.

edits.find: rec: recordings.filter(r => recTitle(r) === norm(s.text)).map(r => r.main.map(n => n.cloneNode(true)))

name: WIP.2 no intro on the table
why: A part's notes are shown between its h3 and its table.

name: WIP.2 disk: introHtml not saved
why: A Load from Disk would lose the part's notes.

name: WIP.2 disk: introHtml not restored
why: Same, on the load side.

name: WIP.2 the native setlist stays
why: The converted paragraph must not stay beside its tables.

name: WIP.2 the native Setlist h2 stays
why: An empty Setlist section would be left behind the tables.

name: WIP.2 setting ignored: setlist
why: Off, the setlist stays as MusicBrainz shows it.

name: WIP.2 setting ignored: setlist one table
why: On, every song goes into one table with a Part column.
grep: One table for the whole setlist

name: WIP.2 no anchor without relationship tables
why: With relationships off, the setlist's own h2 anchors its tables.

edits.find: const anchor = relBuilt ? relH2 : (setGroups.length ? (setH2 || relH2) : null);

name: WIP.2 a song without a work link is dropped
why: A plain-text song line is a row, not a comment.
grep: a song without a work link

name: WIP.3 the section is not stamped with its context
why: Every handler resolves its descriptor from data-mb-art-ctx; unstamped, the event section is treated as the release's (CAA cache, release texts).
grep: only after the button, one request

name: WIP.3 the page's descriptor is always the release's
why: The descriptor must follow the page type, or the event page gets no section at all.
grep: only after the button, one request

name: WIP.3 the event section anchors on the release's tracklist
why: The event page has no h2.tracklist; the section must sit above the event's tables.
grep: only after the button, one request

name: WIP.3 the event setting is ignored
why: Off, no section and no request.
grep: the setting off: no section, no request

name: WIP.3 Spreads offered on the event page
why: Spreads is release packaging; the event layouts are Grid and By type.
grep: Grid / By type only, remembered under the event key

name: WIP.3 the event layout shares the release key
why: An event's types have nothing in common with a release's; its layout is remembered on its own.
grep: Grid / By type only, remembered under the event key

name: WIP.3 the status texts name the Cover Art Archive
why: On the event page the archive is the Event Art Archive, and the thing is an event.

edits.find: status.textContent = `The ${desc.archiveName} has no images for this ${desc.what}.`;
edits.replace: status.textContent = 'The Cover Art Archive has no images for this release.';

name: WIP.3 the tab setting is ignored (both gates)
why: Off, a plain click on the tab must go its normal way. Enforced twice (installing the interceptor, and in the handler) — removing ONE gate cannot be seen, so this entry removes both.
grep: a plain click with the tab setting off

name: WIP.3 'Main back' printed without the flag
why: Event art records have no back flag; "no" would be an invention.

name: WIP.3 the viewer's title is the whole h1
why: After a render the h1 also holds the script's toolbar (and an event's date).

name: 4: '(with …)' not recognised
why: Its artists would be counted as the song's works (a false medley) and get no column.

edits.find: const k = nodes.findIndex(n => n.nodeType === Node.TEXT_NODE && WITH.test(n.textContent));

name: 4: '(with …)' links left as /work/
why: Their MBIDs are artists' (the line-up links the same MBIDs as /artist/).

name: 4: '(with …)' artists not split
why: One row per artist: split at ',', '&' and 'and'.

name: setlist: a note after a blank line becomes a part
why: "Scheduled: 19:00 …" is a note, not a part named after it.
grep: a note right after a blank line

name: setlist: a note before the first part is not carried to it
why: It belongs above the songs that follow it.
grep: a note right after a blank line

name: 5: Song is not a multi-row column
why: Without collapsableColumns the medley's list rows get no toggle.

name: 6: Disambiguation keeps its parentheses
why: The span.comment's own content goes in, without '(' … ')'.
grep: each part of a target line lands in its own column

name: 7: credits not split
why: One row per credit.

name: 7: no Time column
why: "time: …" is its own column, not a credit.
